summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of COPD, CAD s/p CABG, CVA, esophageal stricture, and active alcoholism was admitted for septic shock and multifocal pneumonia following acute hypoxic respiratory failure requiring intubation. He presented with severe dyspnea, aspiration, and septic shock, with labs showing lactic acidosis and acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. He was treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics, vasopressors, and mechanical ventilation. A sputum culture grew Enterobacteriaceae, prompting targeted therapy. After stabilization, he was extubated and transitioned to the medical floor. Due to persistent dysphagia and aspiration on swallow studies, an NJ tube was initially placed, but due to recurrent clogging, a percutaneous endoscopic jejunostomy (PEJ) tube was ultimately placed for long-term nutrition. He improved clinically, with resolution of infection and kidney function, and was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation with plans to reassess swallowing and support alcohol cessation.
